example_input: Add a retry loop to the fetch call in src/api.ts
note: Representations below are simplified shapes of the real types at the pinned SHA, not verbatim dumps.

steps.narrative: The user sends 'Add a retry loop to the fetch call in src/api.ts'. SessionPrompt.prompt() runs revert.cleanup on the session, creates the user message via createUserMessage, touches the session, and — unless noReply — enters loop(), which runs the turn inside state.ensureRunning so concurrent prompts serialize on the session.
steps.title: Input

steps.narrative: runLoop spins while(true). Each iteration: filter compacted messages, take MessageV2.latest() → lastUser/lastAssistant/lastFinished/tasks. Exit only when the last assistant message finished with a non-tool-calls reason AND no pending tool calls AND its parentID is the user message — a 'stop' with tool calls present does NOT exit, so tool results always flow back. The task queue drains first: subtasks via handleSubtask, compactions via compaction.process, overflow via compaction.create(auto:true). Then the agent is resolved, maxSteps (agent.steps ?? Infinity) computed, and the last step injects MAX_STEPS_PROMPT telling the model to wrap up.
steps.title: Loop

steps.narrative: ToolRegistry.tools() builds the tool set for this exact model: websearch only for the opencode provider, and — the distinctive bit — GPT-family models get apply_patch INSTEAD of edit+write (usePatch). The tool.definition plugin hook can rewrite any tool's description/parameters before they're handed to the model. Tool execution stays opencode-owned regardless of which LLM runtime runs below.
steps.title: Tools

steps.narrative: SessionProcessor.create() snapshots the working tree (pre-capture, because the AI SDK may execute tools before emitting events) and builds the ProcessorContext: toolcall map, abort flag, compaction flag. handle.process() then calls LLM.Service with the assembled system prompt (env + instructions + MCP + skills), the message history, and the resolved tools — and adapts the returned event stream into part state transitions (running → completed | error) persisted via sessions.updatePart.
steps.title: Stream

steps.narrative: LLM.Service routes per request through one of two runtimes. Default: the Vercel AI SDK — streamText() runs locally and fullStream is adapted into LLMEvents. Opt-in (OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_NATIVE_LLM): the native runtime lowers the request to an @opencode-ai/llm LLMRequest and executes via LLMClient/RequestExecutor. Both converge on the same LLMEvent stream, so the processor never knows which transport ran. Provider and model come from the live ModelsDev catalog, not a vendored list.
steps.title: Model

steps.narrative: Each tool call hits the permission gate: evaluate() applies last-matching-rule-wins over the layered rulesets (session < approved < agent config), defaulting to ask. A deny fails fast; an ask publishes Permission.Asked on the event bus and parks on a Deferred until the user replies — shutdown fails all pending closed. After edit/write apply, the tool pulls LSP diagnostics and appends any errors to its own output ('LSP errors detected in this file, please fix'), so the model self-corrects next turn without being asked.
steps.title: Execute

steps.narrative: Every message and part lands in SQLite (drizzle, WAL mode) via sessions.updateMessage/updatePart. The loop never holds conversation state in memory across turns — MessageV2.filterCompactedEffect re-reads the working set each iteration, which is what makes interrupt, compaction, and multi-surface (TUI/serve/ACP) concurrency safe.
steps.title: Persist

steps.narrative: Each iteration checks compaction.isOverflow against the model's context budget. On overflow, compaction.create() summarizes the head and keeps a token-estimated recent tail; the loop continues with the compacted history. After the loop breaks, compaction.prune() runs forked in the background. Termination itself is model-driven — there is no fixed iteration cap unless the agent config sets steps.
